children: is giving members of its AAdvantage loyalty program more flexibility to pay for flights as competition among major U.S. carriers for frequent travelers intensifies.

The airline on Friday said eligible AAdvantage members will be able to combine cash and miles when purchasing tickets through its website and mobile app. The feature will roll out in the coming weeks.
Members will first select flights priced in cash. During checkout, American
will display combinations of cash and AAdvantage miles that can be adjusted using a slider. The total price will update based on the mix selected.

The change gives customers another way to use mileage balances without accumulating enough points to cover an entire award ticket. American characterized the feature as part of a broader effort to give AAdvantage members more flexibility in how they use the program.

For investors, the change is significant because airline loyalty programs have evolved into major profit generators and important tools for retaining high-spending customers. Making miles easier to redeem could increase engagement with AAdvantage, encourage spending on American and its credit-card partners and reduce the incentive for customers to shift their loyalty to competing carriers. The tradeoff is that redemption economics matter, so investors will want to see whether greater flexibility drives incremental revenue without materially increasing the cost of rewards.

American has also been expanding AAdvantage benefits. Members reaching 15,000 Loyalty Points can choose two eligible inflight food and beverage coupons, while rewards at various levels now include subscriptions to The New York Times, Games, Cooking and The Athletic. The carrier also plans additional gift choices for customers reaching Million Miler milestones.
The AAdvantage changes arrive as competition for lucrative frequent flyers becomes increasingly aggressive. United Airlines
aimed directly at elite members of American

United is offering qualifying American and Delta customers comparable MileagePlus status for 90 days. Travelers can extend that status through Jan. 31, 2028 by meeting flight and spending requirements during the trial period.

Those requirements range from $1,500 in eligible United spending for travelers seeking its entry-level Premier Silver status to $7,000 for Premier 1K, its highest published elite tier below invitation-only Global Services.

United has promoted the campaign alongside improvements such as Starlink inflight Wi-Fi, explicitly encouraging customers of rival airlines to switch. American, meanwhile, has its own status-match offers for qualifying customers of United, Delta, Southwest Airlines

The competing promotions highlight the value airlines place on loyalty members, particularly travelers who generate revenue not only through tickets but through co-branded credit cards and other program partnerships. American's cash-and-miles feature is less confrontational than United's status-match campaign, but it's part of the same contest: making it harder for valuable customers to find a reason to fly, spend or swipe somewhere else.

title: American Airlines adds cash-and-miles bookings as loyalty battle heats up
